newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: APEC hopes to adopt standards for company disclosure.
newsitem.headline: APEC hopes to adopt standards for company disclosure.

text.p: APEC finance ministers are keen to adopt proposals by the private sector for standardised company disclosure statements, Philippine Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo said on Saturday.
De Ocampo told Reuters that the standardisation proposal was among recommendations presented by the APEC financiers group and AEPC business council over a luncheon with finance ministers.

"The recommmended standardisation in company disclosures will leave less ambiguity in making comparisons, and of course listing across countries could be done on the basis of common understood criteria," said de Ocampo, chairman of the finance ministers' meeting.
The recommendation was accepted in principle by the ministers, he said.
De Ocampo said standardised disclosure statements would help in lining up the divergent accounting procedures of APEC economies.
"The definition of terms should be more global," he said.

The finance secretary said other recommendations by the private sector were the development of a common database on infrastructure projects in APEC economies, enhancement of training of personnel of financial institutions, and a voluntary set of standards to gauge the viability of projects.
The formal set of recommendations would be submitted to the APEC ministers later on Saturday, he said.

Finance ministers of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum were meeting here to forge proposals on initiatives to promote free flow of capital, private participation in infrastructure development and capital market development.

APEC comprises Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, China, Indonesia, Japan, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, Malaysia, Thailand, Taiwan, the Philippines, South Korea, Singapore, Hong Kong and the United States.
The three-day meeting of finance ministers ends Sunday.
